You are one of several READ-ONLY audit agents for the Nxeon customer-portal redesign (Phase 1 = audit only, nothing gets implemented). Codebase: /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15 App Router, React 19, Tailwind v4 with tokens in app/globals.css, Prisma/Postgres, separate worker/ process). Customer portal = app/dashboard/** + components/customer/** + components/portal/Shell.tsx (+ CommandPalette.tsx). API routes live under app/api/**.

HARD RULES: STRICTLY READ-ONLY. Do NOT edit/create/delete ANY file under /opt/nxeon, /opt/nxeon-staging or /opt/nxeon-sandbox. No build, npm, prisma, db, git-write, or service commands. Do not read .env* files or anything that looks like a secret. Your ONLY write is your report file: /tmp/claude-0/-root/1716c7ee-ae35-4cf5-b557-9059709e07c4/scratchpad/audit-01-routes-nav-ia.md (write it with the Write tool). Be exhaustive and factual, cite repo-relative file paths for every claim, use tables, mark anything uncertain as UNVERIFIED. This is an inventory + diagnosis, NOT a design proposal.

YOUR AUDIT: ROUTES / NAVIGATION / INFORMATION ARCHITECTURE.
Produce:
1. COMPLETE customer-facing route inventory. Walk app/dashboard/** recursively (every page.tsx, layout.tsx, loading.tsx, error.tsx, not-found, route groups, dynamic segments). Also find customer-facing routes OUTSIDE app/dashboard: order/checkout/deploy/pricing/login/signup/onboarding/verify/reset/partner/kodely-sso/riddle/whatever exists (list app/* top-level dirs and classify marketing vs portal vs admin vs api). For every portal route give: path pattern, one-line purpose, is it server or client component, main data sources (which API routes / server actions / prisma calls it hits), which feature flags gate it, whether it has loading/error boundaries, and the primary component files it renders.
2. NAVIGATION: dissect components/portal/Shell.tsx fully — sidebar groups + items + order + icons + badges + collapsed behaviour + which items are conditional (feature flags, account state, roles), top bar contents (search, notifications, account menu, currency, support), mobile behaviour, footer/support layer, any secondary nav (tabs inside product areas). Also dissect CommandPalette.tsx: what it indexes, categories, keyboard shortcuts, actions.
3. In-page sub-navigation: for each product area (servers, games, hosting, sites, domains, email/mail, volumes, nxcloud, build, projects, claude-code, migrate, tools, billing, settings, team, support) list the tabs/sections and how they're implemented (tabs component? query param? nested routes?). Note inconsistencies in tab implementation.
4. OVERLAP MAP: the known confusing overlap is servers vs games vs hosting vs sites vs build vs projects vs claude-code vs nxcloud vs volumes vs matrix vs deploy vs order vs tools. For each, state precisely what it is, what backend concept it maps to, what it shares with the others, and where a customer would be confused. Identify dead/legacy/redirect-only routes.
5. Middleware / redirects / auth gating: read middleware.ts and any redirects in next.config; list route-level auth and role requirements (team roles, partner, etc.).
6. Entry points into purchase flows: every link/button that starts a purchase or deploy (from dashboard, sidebar, empty states, marketing) and where it goes.
7. Diagnosis section: IA problems observed (duplication, naming inconsistency, orphan pages, depth issues, mixed mental models), with evidence.
Finish by writing the report, then reply with a ~10-line summary including the total route count and the top 5 IA problems.
